Classification rationale: Holds highly sensitive customer personal, financial and transaction data; disclosure could cause fraud, regulatory penalties and reputational damage
Threat: Unauthorised administrative access and data theft
Vulnerability: No MFA on admin accounts, shared administrator passwords, no alerts for unusual access
Treatment rationale: Strong access controls reduce the likelihood of unauthorised access
Control 1: Enforce MFA on admin accounts and stop password sharing among IT staff
Control 2: Log all database access and alert on unusual admin activity

Classification rationale: Gives access to customer wallets, authentication data and transactions; compromise leads directly to account takeover and unauthorised transfers
Threat: Account takeover, credential stuffing and unauthorised transfers
Vulnerability: No customer MFA, no login rate limiting, weak monitoring of suspicious activity
Treatment rationale: Authentication and monitoring controls reduce account-takeover risk
Control 2: Apply login rate limiting, temporary account lockouts and suspicious-transaction monitoring

Classification rationale: Vendor assessments, contracts, system access details and data-sharing arrangements are sensitive business information for authorised parties only
Threat: Third-party data breach and unauthorised disclosure
Vulnerability: No formal vendor security assessment; data-sharing boundaries poorly documented
Treatment rationale: Vendor assessment before onboarding, contractual security controls and continuous monitoring reduce third-party risk
Control 1: Carry out a vendor security assessment and schedule regular vendor-risk reviews
Control 2: Set up secure data-sharing arrangements limited to authorised parties
